level.title: Hindi A1+ — Getting around
goals: Ask for directions, tickets and things you need
Give a phone number, an address and a price
Make a plan and refuse one politely

lessons.title: Directions: सीधे, बाएँ, दाएँ
lessons.learn: Directions are all polite imperatives, so they end in -इए: सीधे जाइए (go straight), बाएँ मुड़िए (turn left), दाएँ मुड़िए (turn right). Landmarks carry their own postpositions: सामने (in front), पीछे (behind), पास (near), दूर (far) — and each one follows the noun it describes.

grammar.title: Route instructions in -इए
grammar.explain: Every step of a route is a polite imperative: पहले सीधे जाइए, फिर बाएँ मुड़िए, फिर दाएँ. The landmark comes before its postposition: बैंक के सामने (in front of the bank), स्टेशन के पास (near the station).
grammar.pattern: सीधे जाइए · बाएँ/दाएँ मुड़िए · X के सामने/पीछे/पास

examples.en: The bank is in front of the market.

examples.t: स्टेशन यहाँ से दूर नहीं है।
examples.r: sṭeśan yahāṅ se dūr nahīṅ hai.
examples.en: The station is not far from here.

mistakes.wrong: सीधे जाओ, बाएँ मुड़ो। (to a stranger)
mistakes.why: directions to a stranger take the -इए form. जाओ/मुड़ो are for people you call तुम.

dialogue.en: Excuse me, where is the market?
Go straight, then turn left.
How far is it?

dialogue.t: ज़्यादा दूर नहीं — बस के पास ही है।
dialogue.r: zyādā dūr nahīṅ — bas ke pās hī hai.
dialogue.en: Not far — it is right next to the bus stop.

lessons.title: Transport: बस, ऑटो, टिकट
lessons.learn: Transport words and the two postpositions that run a journey: से (from) and तक (up to). दिल्ली से जयपुर तक (from Delhi to Jaipur). To ask where someone is going: आप कहाँ जा रहे हैं? For a ticket: एक टिकट चाहिए.

grammar.title: X से Y तक
grammar.explain: से marks the starting point and तक the end, and they wrap the journey: जयपुर से दिल्ली तक. The verb agrees with the subject, not the route: गाड़ी कितने बजे चलती है? (when does the train leave?)
grammar.pattern: X से Y तक · … चाहिए · कहाँ जाना है?

examples.t: जयपुर से दिल्ली तक कितना किराया है?
examples.r: Jaipur se Dillī tak kitnā kirāyā hai?
examples.en: What is the fare from Jaipur to Delhi?
What time does the train leave?

mistakes.why: चाहिए is invariable and the person takes the को-form: मुझे चाहिए. चाहता हूँ exists but means 'I want' with a different frame, and it is not what you say at a counter.

dialogue.t: जयपुर से दिल्ली तक कितना किराया है?
dialogue.r: Jaipur se Dillī tak kitnā kirāyā hai?
dialogue.en: What is the fare from Jaipur to Delhi?

dialogue.t: बस का चार सौ, गाड़ी का सात सौ।
dialogue.r: bas kā cār sau, gāṛī kā sāt sau.
dialogue.en: Four hundred by bus, seven hundred by train.
I need two bus tickets.

dialogue.t: गाड़ी सुबह छह बजे चलती है — आपको जल्दी पहुँचना है।
dialogue.r: gāṛī subah chah baje caltī hai — āpko jaldī pahuṅcnā hai.
dialogue.en: The bus leaves at six in the morning — you need to arrive early.

lessons.title: मुझे … चाहिए — asking for things
lessons.learn: The single most useful A1+ sentence is मुझे … चाहिए: मुझे पानी चाहिए, मुझे मदद चाहिए, मुझे एक कमरा चाहिए. The person takes को (मुझे/आपको/उसे), the thing is plain, and चाहिए never changes. Add माफ़ कीजिए in front and it works at any counter.

grammar.title: मुझे X चाहिए
grammar.explain: The frame is fixed: person in the को-form, thing in the plain form, चाहिए unchanged. मुझे एक कमरा चाहिए (I want a room), आपको क्या चाहिए? (what do you want?). Nothing about the thing changes चाहिए — not its gender, not its number.

mistakes.why: चाहिए never takes मैं. The wanting happens *to* you in Hindi — the same को-form as मुझे पसंद है.

dialogue.t: माफ़ कीजिए, मुझे एक कमरा चाहिए।
dialogue.r: māf kījie, mujhe ek kamrā cāhie.
dialogue.en: Excuse me, I need a room.
For one night?
Yes — and I need water as well.

dialogue.t: जी, कमरा नंबर तीन। कोई और चीज़ चाहिए?
dialogue.r: jī, kamrā nambar tīn. koī aur cīz cāhie?
dialogue.en: Yes, room three. Anything else?

Practice 4: [reverse translation] मुझे … चाहिए — asking for things — Write in Devanagari: What would you like?.

lessons.title: Numbers 20–100
lessons.learn: Hindi numbers up to twenty are irregular and have to be learned as sounds; from twenty on they are built, but in a way English does not prepare you for: पचास is literally 'half of a hundred', and इक्कीस is 'twenty-and-one' with the units first. Practice them aloud in order — the rhythm is half the memory.

grammar.title: Units before tens from 21 up
grammar.explain: From twenty-one to ninety-nine the units come first and are joined with और: इक्कीस is one-and-twenty. पचास (50) and सत्तर (70) are the two odd ones to memorise. From fifty, the units sit inside the word: पचपन (55), पचहत्तर (75), नब्बे (90).

examples.en: The train will arrive in fifty minutes.
There are seventy-five people in the room.

mistakes.why: from fifty up the unit is inside the word. पचास पाँच is not a number anyone says — it will be heard as two numbers.

dialogue.en: This kurta is eighty.

dialogue.t: अस्सी बहुत है — सत्तर में दीजिए।
dialogue.r: assī bahut hai — sattar meṅ dījie.
dialogue.en: Eighty is a lot — give it for seventy.
Seventy-five — final word.

dialogue.t: ठीक है, सौ का नोट दीजिए ग़लत नहीं।
dialogue.r: ṭhīk hai, sau kā noṭ dījie ġalat nahīṅ.
dialogue.en: Fine — a hundred-rupee note, mind the change.

lessons.title: Phone numbers and addresses
lessons.learn: A phone number is read digit by digit, and Indians say zero as ज़ीरो or शून्य. To ask for a repeat: ज़रा दोबारा बताइए. An address needs the noun chain पता (address), सड़क (road), मोहल्ला (locality), मकान (house) — and the postposition at the end: सड़क पर, मोहल्ले में.

grammar.title: Digit by digit, and ज़रा … बताइए
grammar.explain: Phone numbers are read as separate digits: नौ, आठ, दो… To ask for a repeat, ज़रा दोबारा बताइए (could you tell me again). For an address the postposition closes the phrase: मकान नंबर बारह, नई सड़क पर.
grammar.pattern: मेरा नंबर … है · ज़रा दोबारा बताइए · … सड़क पर

examples.t: मेरा मकान नई सड़क पर है।
examples.r: merā makān naī saṛak par hai.
examples.en: My house is on Nai Road.

mistakes.wrong: मैं आपको फ़ोन करना चाहता हूँ। (asking for the number)
mistakes.right: आपका नंबर मिल सकता है? / मुझे आपका नंबर चाहिए।
mistakes.why: the English sentence states your intention; Hindi asks for the number. Saying your wish instead of your request sounds like a statement, not a question.

dialogue.en: What is your phone number?
Nine-eight-two-zero-four…
Sorry, could you say that again?
Nine-eight-two-zero-four. And your address?

lessons.title: Prices and paying
lessons.learn: Money words carry gender: रुपया is masculine, पैसा masculine, and रुपये is the plural you actually use — पचास रुपये. To ask the total: कुल कितना हुआ? Card or cash: कार्ड चलेगा या नक़द? छुट्टा means exact change, and every shop will ask you for it.

grammar.title: कुल कितना हुआ? · चलेगा?
grammar.explain: कुल कितना हुआ? asks the total after the fact — हुआ, not है, because the bill has already built up. चलेगा? is the everyday way to ask whether a method of payment is accepted: कार्ड चलेगा? छुट्टा है? asks whether you have small change, and the answer is usually नहीं.
grammar.pattern: कुल कितना हुआ? · कार्ड चलेगा? · छुट्टा नहीं है

examples.t: यह बहुत महँगा है, थोड़ा सस्ता कीजिए।
examples.r: yah bahut mahṅgā hai, thoṛā sastā kījie.
examples.en: This is too expensive, make it a little cheaper.

mistakes.right: यह बहुत महँगा है। / यह पचास रुपये का है।

lessons.title: Weather and small talk
lessons.learn: Weather is the safest small talk in India and it runs on two nouns: गर्मी (heat) and सर्दी (cold), used with है — आज बहुत गर्मी है. For the outdoors: धूप (sunshine), बारिश (rain), हवा (wind), बादल (cloud). बारिश हो रही है for rain falling now.

grammar.title: गर्मी है · बारिश हो रही है
grammar.explain: Heat and cold are nouns with है: आज बहुत गर्मी है. Rain, however, is an event: बारिश हो रही है (it is raining), बारिश होगी (it will rain). ठंडा agrees with the thing that is cold: पानी ठंडा है, चाय ठंडी है.
grammar.pattern: गर्मी/सर्दी है · बारिश हो रही है · X ठंडा/ठंडी है

examples.t: बारिश हो रही है — छाता लीजिए।
examples.r: bāriś ho rahī hai — chhātā lījie.
examples.en: It is raining — take an umbrella.

mistakes.wrong: आज बहुत गर्म है। (about the weather)
mistakes.why: गर्म describes a thing (यह कमरा गर्म है); गर्मी is the noun for weather. The noun is what a conversation about the day uses.

dialogue.en: It is very hot today!

dialogue.t: हाँ, और शाम को बारिश होगी।
dialogue.r: hāṅ, aur śām ko bāriś hogī.
dialogue.en: Yes, and it will rain in the evening.
Then keep an umbrella.

dialogue.t: ज़रूर। सर्दी में यह मौसम बहुत अच्छा होता है।
dialogue.r: zarūr. sardī meṅ yah mausam bahut achchhā hotā hai.
dialogue.en: Certainly. In winter this weather is very good.

lessons.title: Making a plan: कब मिलेंगे?
lessons.learn: To arrange something: कब मिलेंगे? (when shall we meet?), मैं आज़ाद हूँ (I am free), मैं व्यस्त हूँ (I am busy), और मुझे … बजे आना है (I have to come at …). इंतज़ार करना is to wait, and माफ़ी for a small apology — the daily grammar of keeping an appointment in India.

grammar.title: कब मिलेंगे? · मुझे … बजे आना है
grammar.explain: मिलेंगे is the future with the respectful plural ending, so it fits any company: हम कब मिलेंगे? 'Have to' is the infinitive plus है: मुझे छह बजे आना है (I have to come at six) — the person takes को again.
grammar.pattern: कब मिलेंगे? · मुझे + time + आना है · समय तय कीजिए

examples.en: I have to come at six.

examples.t: कल शाम का समय तय कर लीजिए।
examples.r: kal śām kā samay tay kar lījie.
examples.en: Let us fix a time for tomorrow evening.

mistakes.why: 'have to' puts the person in the को-form. मैं आना है is two subjects in one sentence and is heard as a mistake.

dialogue.en: When shall we meet?
This evening? I am free.

dialogue.t: माफ़ कीजिए, आज मैं व्यस्त हूँ। कल?
dialogue.r: māf kījie, āj main vyast hūṅ. kal?
dialogue.en: Sorry, I am busy today. Tomorrow?

dialogue.t: ठीक है — मुझे पाँच बजे आना है, छह बजे मिल लेंगे।
dialogue.r: ṭhīk hai — mujhe pāṅc baje ānā hai, chah baje mil leṅge.
dialogue.en: All right — I have to come at five, we will meet at six.

lessons.title: Saying no politely
lessons.learn: A refusal in Hindi arrives wrapped: माफ़ कीजिए, मैं नहीं आ पाऊँगा (sorry, I will not be able to come). The compound नहीं … पाना is what makes it 'will not be able' rather than 'will not', and it is much softer. Close with अगली बार ज़रूर (next time, certainly) and the door stays open.

grammar.title: नहीं + पाना = 'will not be able'
grammar.explain: पाना as the second verb adds ability: आ पाना (to be able to come), कर पाना (to manage to do). Made negative it becomes the polite refusal — मैं नहीं आ पाऊँगा — where plain मैं नहीं आऊँगा sounds like a door closing. मजबूरी है ('it is a compulsion') is the standard reason and needs no details.
grammar.pattern: माफ़ कीजिए, मैं … नहीं … पाऊँगा · अगली बार ज़रूर

examples.t: माफ़ कीजिए, मैं नहीं आ पाऊँगा।
examples.r: māf kījie, main nahīṅ ā pāūṅgā.
examples.en: Sorry, I will not be able to come.
It is unavoidable — next time, certainly.

mistakes.wrong: नहीं, मैं नहीं आऊँगा। (to a colleague)
mistakes.right: माफ़ कीजिए, मैं नहीं आ पाऊँगा।
mistakes.why: the bare future refuses the event; नहीं … पाना refuses the possibility, which is what politeness needs. The apology in front is not optional.

dialogue.en: Will you come to tomorrow's meeting?

dialogue.t: माफ़ कीजिए, मैं नहीं आ पाऊँगी।
dialogue.r: māf kījie, main nahīṅ ā pāūṅgī.
dialogue.en: Sorry, I will not be able to come.
No matter — the reason?

dialogue.t: मजबूरी है। कोशिश करूँगी — अगली बार ज़रूर।
dialogue.r: majbūrī hai. kośiś karūṅgī — aglī bār zarūr.
dialogue.en: It is unavoidable. I will try — next time, certainly.

items.q: Choose the polite direction to a stranger: turn left.

items.answer: जयपुर से दिल्ली तक कितना किराया है?

items.answer: refusing politely and leaving the door open

items.q: आज बहुत गर्मी है, और शाम को बारिश होगी। What is this about?
मेरा मकान नई सड़क पर है। Where is the house?

culture.text: हाँ जी and अच्छा are the two words that hold up an Indian conversation. हाँ जी is not ‘yes sir’ — जी is a politeness particle that can follow almost anything (नहीं जी, ठीक जी, प्रकाश जी), and it is what you say on the phone to mean 'yes, I am listening'. अच्छा is 'I see' / 'really?', and the length of it tells you how surprised the speaker is. A learner who can say हाँ जी and अच्छा at the right moments sounds attentive long before their grammar is ready.

reading.text: सुबह आठ बजे हैं। प्रकाश बस स्टैंड पर खड़ा है। उसे दिल्ली जाना है। वह क्लर्क से पूछता है, “दिल्ली की बस कितने बजे आएगी?” क्लर्क कहता है, “आधे घंटे में। टिकट लीजिए — चार सौ रुपये।” प्रकाश के पास सौ का नोट है। वह कहता है, “माफ़ कीजिए, छुट्टा है?” क्लर्क हँसता है और कहता है, “नहीं, पाँच सौ दीजिए।” प्रकाश पाँच सौ देता है और बस में बैठ जाता है।
reading.gloss: It is eight in the morning. Prakash is standing at the bus stand. He has to go to Delhi. He asks the clerk, “When will the Delhi bus come?” The clerk says, “In half an hour. Take a ticket — four hundred rupees.” Prakash has a hundred-rupee note. He says, “Excuse me, do you have change?” The clerk laughs and says, “No, give me five hundred.” Prakash gives five hundred and sits down in the bus.

listening.script:
— माफ़ कीजिए, स्टेशन कहाँ है?
— सीधे जाइए, फिर बाएँ मुड़िए। ज़्यादा दूर नहीं है।
— धन्यवाद! और टिकट कहाँ मिलेगा?
— खिड़की नंबर दो पर। मुझे पाँच बजे की गाड़ी पकड़नी है, जल्दी कीजिए।
— जी, बहुत धन्यवाद।
listening.gloss:
— Excuse me, where is the station?
— Go straight, then turn left. It is not far.
— Thank you! And where do I get a ticket?
— At window two. I have to catch the five o'clock train, hurry.
— Yes, thank you very much.

idioms.meaning: yes — and also 'I am listening' on the phone
I see / really? — the more drawn out, the more surprised
never mind — the standard answer to an apology
hold on a moment — a polite pause, not a refusal
excuse me — before asking a stranger anything
come on — the respectful invitation to move on
how nice! — on hearing somebody's news
see you — with no date attached
relax — also a polite way to stall
just a moment — never literally a minute

mistakes.why: the person phoned takes को, not से — से would mean 'from'. फ़ोन करना is one of the first verbs where the postposition has to be learned with the verb.
चाहिए never agrees with anything. Dropping the को-form or agreeing the verb is the commonest A1+ slip.
बस is feminine, so its verb is आएगी. Bus, train, car and plane are all feminine in Hindi — गाड़ी is the umbrella word, and it is feminine.

task.title: Plan a journey out loud
task.instructions: Write and then say aloud a six-line journey plan: where you are going, how, at what time, what it costs, and one thing you will ask a stranger. Use से … तक for the route, मुझे … चाहिए at least once, and one polite refusal or apology. Say it twice — the second time with the page face down and without stopping to correct yourself.
